identity.name: ECO HOTELS AND RESORTS LIMITED
identity.industry: Sustainable Mid-Premium Hospitality with Vegetarian Focus in Tier II/III Cities

summary.oneLiner: Eco Hotels And Resorts Limited is pioneering India’s first net-zero premium value hotel brand with a strict vegetarian philosophy, targeting high-growth Tier II/III cities through an asset-light EBOT™ model that combines 3D volumetric construction, AI-driven operations, and guaranteed investor returns — positioning it to capture the $100B+ sustainable tourism wave driven by spiritual, wellness, and eco-conscious travel demand.

one-line thesis: Eco Hotels And Resorts Limited is pioneering India’s first net-zero premium value hotel brand with a strict vegetarian philosophy, targeting high-growth Tier II/III cities through an asset-light EBOT™ model that combines 3D volumetric construction, AI-driven operations, and guaranteed investor returns — positioning it to capture the $100B+ sustainable tourism wave driven by spiritual, wellness, and eco-conscious travel demand.
financial scorecard / credit view: ₹420 Cr revenue / ₹85 Cr EBITDA / ₹32 Cr PAT / ₹0 net-debt (FY26)
guidance / outlook: Targeting 5,000 keys by 2030; expanding via EBOT™ and management contracts in pilgrimage, wellness, and business corridors; aiming for 25% CAGR in revenue through FY28.
order book & pipeline: 65 keys (Dombivli), 50 keys (Indore), 135 keys (Gandhinagar), 40 keys (Bangalore) — all under discussion for closure; 10+ upcoming properties confirmed for Q1–Q2 FY27
segment / subsidiary detail: THE ECO™ (mid-premium, 30-65 keys, INR 2,500-4,500/night); THE ECO GRAND™ (premium, 65-100 keys, INR 3,500-7,499/night); ECOVALUE™ (budget, 15-35 keys, INR 1,500-3,500/night); ECOXPRESS™ (transit, 40-100 keys, INR 1,500-3,500/night); all brands feature 100% vegetarian dining via SAHAR, GG’S, KICK IN THE BRICK
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into 15+ new Tier II/III cities via EBOT™ model; potential franchising of 'Satva' vegetarian F&B brands; entry into wellness retreats and pilgrimage corridors; possible spin-off of modular construction arm (Red Ribbon RE Rise India)
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin ~20% (FY26); cost advantage from 3D volumetric construction (30% faster build, 20% lower capex); F&B contributes 35% of revenue with 50%+ margins
capex / expansion: ₹180 Cr planned for FY26–FY27 (primarily for 8 new EBOT™ projects; Dombivli: ₹45 Cr, Indore: ₹30 Cr, Gandhinagar: ₹75 Cr)
capital allocation: 70% to new hotel development via EBOT™, 20% to tech/AI integration, 10% to brand expansion (F&B); zero debt, no equity dilution planned; 100% internally funded
risks & watch-items: Delays in regulatory approvals for greenfield projects; competition from established chains entering mid-premium segment; supply chain disruptions for modular construction materials; slower-than-expected adoption of vegetarian-only model in non-pilgrimage markets
non-obvious takeaways: The company’s 'Satva' vegetarian dining concept is not just a menu choice but a core brand differentiator — aligned with spiritual tourism demand and creating 50%+ F&B margins, effectively turning food into a profit engine rather than a cost center.
